66:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَۖ تَبۡتَغِي مَرۡضَاتَ أَزۡوَٰجِكَۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
66:1.en: O Prophet! Why bannest thou that which Allah hath made lawful for thee, seeking to please thy wives? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

66:2.ar: قَدۡ فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ تَحِلَّةَ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
66:2.en: Allah hath made lawful for you (Muslims) absolution from your oaths (of such a kind), and Allah is your Protector. He is the Knower, the Wise

66:3.ar: وَإِذۡ أَسَرَّ ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضِ أَزۡوَٰجِهِۦ حَدِيثࣰ ا فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتۡ بِهِۦ وَأَظۡهَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ عَرَّفَ بَعۡضَهُۥ وَأَعۡرَضَ عَنۢ بَعۡضࣲۖ فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَهَا بِهِۦ قَالَتۡ مَنۡ أَنۢبَأَكَ هَٰذَاۖ قَالَ نَبَّأَنِيَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
66:3.en: When the Prophet confided a fact unto one of his wives and when she afterward divulged it and Allah apprised him thereof, he made known (to her) part thereof and passed over part. And when he told it her she said: Who hath told thee? He said: The Knower, the Aware hath told me

5:89.ar: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغۡوِ فِيٓ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلۡأَيۡمَٰنَۖ فَكَفَّٰرَتُهُۥٓ إِطۡعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَٰكِينَ مِنۡ أَوۡسَطِ مَا تُطۡعِمُونَ أَهۡلِيكُمۡ أَوۡ كِسۡوَتُهُمۡ أَوۡ تَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةࣲۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامࣲۚ ذَٰلِكَ كَفَّٰرَةُ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ إِذَا حَلَفۡتُمۡۚ وَٱحۡفَظُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
5:89.en: Allah will not take you to task for that which is unintentional in your oaths, but He will take you to task for the oaths which ye swear in earnest. The expiation thereof is the feeding of ten of the needy with the average of that wherewith ye feed your own folk, or the clothing of them, or the liberation of a slave, and for him who findeth not (the wherewithal to do so) then a three days' fast. This is the expiation of your oaths when ye have sworn; and keep your oaths. Thus Allah expoundeth unto you His revelations in order that ye may give thanks

7:32.ar: قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِۚ قُلۡ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا خَالِصَةࣰ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:32.en: Say: Who hath forbidden the adornment of Allah which He hath brought forth for His bondmen, and the good things of His providing? Say: Such, on the Day of Resurrection, will be only for those who believed during the life of the world. Thus do we detail Our revelations for people who have knowledge

G9q6ifi0VpI.title: Surat At-Tahrim, Part 1: Verses 1-3
G9q6ifi0VpI.one_line: The honey incident teaches three household lessons: do not give up lawful things just to please a spouse, keep family confidences, and stop needing to be right.
G9q6ifi0VpI.summary: Opening At-Tahrim, the last of the organizational Madinan cluster, he explains that marriage makes you a household, the basic unit of the ummah, so the collective reflects its homes. He warns that applying these verses without accounting for our context breeds individual extremism. He then gives context for the Prophet's marriages: decades of monogamy and chastity, wives mostly widows from rival tribes and faiths, and mothers of the believers whose religious, political and social immunity preserved women's gains, with Aisha the main source on his character. In the honey story, two wives claimed his breath smelled so he would stop visiting Zaynab, and he swore off honey. Allah's rebuke teaches that giving up something lawful and harmless to please a spouse plants resentment; forbidding the lawful is as serious as permitting the forbidden, and couples should discuss expectations before marriage. The leaked secret teaches confidentiality: keep problems inside the home, away from parents, friends and social media. The Prophet raised only the breach of trust and let the plot pass, showing that marriage is about compassion, not being right. He asks couples to compromise wisely, guard privacy and let small things go.

outline.heading: The four clusters of the final juz
outline.gist: The comprehensive surahs fall into four groups; this session begins the last surah of the second, organizational cluster.

outline.heading: An organizational, Madinan cluster
outline.gist: Revealed when the Prophet had authority in Madinah, these surahs organize relationships; the last ones dealt with marriage and divorce.

outline.heading: Marriage makes you a household
outline.gist: With or without children, a married couple becomes a bayt, the basic Islamic unit that builds the ummah.

outline.heading: The collective is its households
outline.gist: A country is millions of households; when we zoom out we forget that people just want stable homes.

outline.heading: Drawing analogies across different contexts
outline.gist: We do not live in a Muslim state, so applying these late Madinan verses requires accounting for the differences.

outline.heading: Context-free reading breeds individual extremism
outline.gist: A new Muslim reading verses on fighting without context can go astray; bearing arms outside a state's army is forbidden in Islamic law.

outline.heading: A pragmatic text, unlike constitutions
outline.gist: Few people read constitutions; the Quran was revealed through the Prophet's life so we can learn practical lessons.

outline.heading: Organized, but told dynamically
outline.gist: Each cluster and surah covers a topic from an angle, through stories rather than numbered articles, to keep us reflecting.

outline.heading: Interlude
Context: the Prophet's marriages
outline.gist: He was married only to Khadijah for 25 years, then to the elderly widow Sawdah; later marriages, commanded by Allah, joined tribes and faiths.

outline.heading: Mothers of the believers and their immunity
outline.gist: They held religious, political and social immunity; Aisha even led an army, unprecedented for a woman.

outline.heading: Regression after the leader: the zakat refusal
outline.gist: When a core leader dies people revert, as tribes refused to send zakat to the centre after the Prophet.

outline.heading: How his wives protected women's gains
outline.gist: As teachers they kept women educated after centuries of being treated as property; the divorce verses likewise protected women.

outline.heading: Not a womanizer: chastity and monogamy
outline.gist: He stayed chaste until 25 when others married at 13, and monogamous until his fifties; desire does not begin at 55.

outline.heading: The pattern of whom he married
outline.gist: Most were widows or divorcees from every major tribe, a pattern of reconciliation rather than beauty.

outline.heading: Aisha, chief witness to his character
outline.gist: With full immunity she could have said anything; instead most narrations of his kindness and patience come from her.

outline.heading: The honey and the plot
outline.gist: He stopped at one wife's home for honey; two others agreed to tell him his breath smelled of a foul plant the bees fed on.

outline.heading: He swore off honey
outline.gist: When both said it he vowed never to eat it again; they knew how much he cared about hygiene.

outline.heading: The Prophet's hygiene: miswak, garlic and onion
outline.gist: He made tooth cleaning part of worship and avoided raw garlic and onion so as not to bother people or angels.

outline.heading: Eat considerately before coming to the masjid
outline.gist: Heavy, spicy meals before Ramadan prayers bother those beside you; eat lightly, pray, then eat.

outline.heading: Why forbid what Allah made lawful for you?
outline.gist: The verse rebukes him for forbidding himself something lawful to please his wives, which does not mean never seek a spouse's pleasure.

outline.heading: Unnecessary sacrifice plants resentment
outline.gist: Giving up something lawful, harmless and loved for a spouse is a speck that grows into resentment over years.

outline.heading: Expiating a broken oath
outline.gist: Allah ordained release from oaths: feed ten poor people or fast three days; he was told to break it and enjoy the honey.

outline.heading: Discuss expectations before marriage
outline.gist: Talking upfront reveals different expectations so couples can decide what to give up or find middle ground.

outline.heading: Forbidding the lawful is as serious as allowing the forbidden
outline.gist: Who forbade the adornments Allah allowed? Over-prohibiting seems safe but eventually floods the gates as a generation rebels.

outline.heading: Haram means sacred
outline.gist: Only the Holy One can declare something forbidden; letting others do so unbalances the mind.

outline.heading: The husband and wife who give up their lives
outline.gist: A man who drops friends and sport, or a woman cut off from family or education, will come to resent the spouse.

outline.heading: Allah intervened so he would not teach it
outline.gist: The Prophet was selfless and ascetic so it cost him little, but his followers would be harmed by imitating it.

outline.heading: Their sacrifice becomes your debt
outline.gist: If your spouse gives up what they love for you, you carry a burden you can never repay.

outline.heading: Why would this be in the Quran?
outline.gist: Orientalists asked why he would invent verses for honey; it makes sense only as Allah teaching through the incident.

outline.heading: What married people regret giving up
outline.gist: Most couples recall what they gave up or made the other give up; compatibility and frank talk prevent it.

outline.heading: Interlude
The confided secret that spread
outline.gist: He asked one wife to keep his vow private; she told another, and the story is narrated by Umar, whose daughter was involved.

outline.heading: The Quran does not name those at fault
outline.gist: As in the Sunnah, mistakes are told without naming people, to teach rather than shame.

outline.heading: He mentioned part and passed over part
outline.gist: He only told her to keep his confidences, never mentioning the plot, which they learned of only when he recited these verses in prayer.

outline.heading: Solve problems inside the home
outline.gist: Bringing others in, especially parents, usually makes things worse because they have their own agendas.

outline.heading: Know what abuse is
outline.gist: Women should learn a sound definition of abuse before marriage, neither ignoring it nor calling every disagreement abuse; abuse must be reported, other issues resolved privately.

outline.heading: Keep your household's secrets
outline.gist: We compare and judge whatever we hear about other homes, which breeds discontent in our own.

outline.heading: Live-streaming private life
outline.gist: People broadcasting what happens inside their homes, and others watching, is a sign of how far things have gone.

outline.heading: Marriage is not about being right
outline.gist: Those always right end up alone; jealousy is often a form of love and does not need correcting.

outline.heading: Correct only what affects the home
outline.gist: He addressed only the breach of trust; told by the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, names covering even unspoken intentions.

outline.heading: Lesson one: be careful what you give up
outline.gist: Compromise is important, but do not give up lawful things needlessly or let your spouse do so.

outline.heading: Lesson two: keep confidences
outline.gist: Keep private matters within the home, especially away from parents.

outline.heading: Lesson three: compassion over being right
outline.gist: Understand the other's angle and let unimportant things go; people remember when their mistakes are not held against them.

14:5.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أَنۡ أَخۡرِجۡ قَوۡمَكَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ وَذَكِّرۡهُم بِأَيَّىٰمِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارࣲ شَكُورࣲ‏
14:5.en: We verily sent Moses with Our revelations, saying: Bring thy people forth from darkness unto light. And remind them of the days of Allah. Lo! therein are revelations for each steadfast, thankful (heart)

2:44.ar: ۞أَتَأۡمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلۡبِرِّ وَتَنسَوۡنَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ تَتۡلُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
2:44.en: Enjoin ye righteousness upon mankind while ye yourselves forget (to practise it)? And ye are readers of the Scripture! Have ye then no sense

4:66.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّا كَتَبۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنِ ٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱخۡرُجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِكُم مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فَعَلُواْ مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَشَدَّ تَثۡبِيتࣰ ا
4:66.en: And if We had decreed for them: Lay down your lives or go forth from your dwellings, but few of them would have done it; though if they did what they are exhorted to do it would be better for them, and more strengthening

4:67.ar: وَإِذࣰ ا لَّأٓتَيۡنَٰهُم مِّن لَّدُنَّآ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:67.en: And then We should bestow upon them from Our presence an immense reward

4:68.en: And should guide them unto a straight path

57:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتُ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱنظُرُونَا نَقۡتَبِسۡ مِن نُّورِكُمۡ قِيلَ ٱرۡجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمۡ فَٱلۡتَمِسُواْ نُورࣰ اۖ فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَهُم بِسُورࣲ لَّهُۥ بَابُۢ بَاطِنُهُۥ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةُ وَظَٰهِرُهُۥ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ
57:13.en: On the day when the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will say unto those who believe: Look on us that we may borrow from your light! it will be said: Go back and seek for light! Then there will separate them a wall wherein is a gate, the inner side whereof containeth mercy, while the outer side thereof is toward the doom

14:4.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسَانِ قَوۡمِهِۦ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمۡۖ فَيُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
14:4.en: And We never sent a messenger save with the language of his folk, that he might make (the message) clear for them. Then Allah sendeth whom He will astray, and guideth whom He will. He is the Mighty, the Wise

16:125.ar: ٱدۡعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلۡحِكۡمَةِ وَٱلۡمَوۡعِظَةِ ٱلۡحَسَنَةِۖ وَجَٰدِلۡهُم بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
16:125.en: Call unto the way of thy Lord with wisdom and fair exhortation, and reason with them in the better way. Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth from His way, and He is Best Aware of those who go aright

71:5.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوۡتُ قَوۡمِي لَيۡلࣰ ا وَنَهَارࣰ ا
71:5.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! I have called unto my people night and day

71:6.ar: فَلَمۡ يَزِدۡهُمۡ دُعَآءِيٓ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
71:6.en: But all my calling doth but add to their repugnance

71:7.ar: وَإِنِّي كُلَّمَا دَعَوۡتُهُمۡ لِتَغۡفِرَ لَهُمۡ جَعَلُوٓاْ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡشَوۡاْ ثِيَابَهُمۡ وَأَصَرُّواْ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ ٱسۡتِكۡبَارࣰ ا
71:7.en: And lo! whenever I call unto them that Thou mayst pardon them they thrust their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments and persist (in their refusal) and magnify themselves in pride

71:8.en: And lo! I have called unto them aloud

71:9.ar: ثُمَّ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَنتُ لَهُمۡ وَأَسۡرَرۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِسۡرَارࣰ ا
71:9.en: And lo! I have made public proclamation unto them, and I have appealed to them in private

71:10.ar: فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارࣰ ا
71:10.en: And I have said: Seek pardon of your Lord. Lo! He was ever Forgiving

71:11.en: He will let loose the sky for you in plenteous rain

71:12.ar: وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٰلࣲ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡهَٰرࣰ ا
71:12.en: And will help you with wealth and sons, and will assign unto you Gardens and will assign unto you rivers

w8zz_zRXjWE.speaker_note: Single speaker; continues 'the series that I am sharing with you' for the masjid's August outreach month and refers to 'last week' of the same series.
w8zz_zRXjWE.title: Outreach, The Way of Our Prophets: Practising and Sharing Enlightenment
w8zz_zRXjWE.one_line: Two conditions for dawah from Surah Ibrahim: see Islam as light and live it yourself first, then speak to people in a language they understand.
w8zz_zRXjWE.summary: Continuing the outreach month, he admits it is hard to speak of dawah while Gaza burns; the one lesson he will name now is that international law seems to bind only people like us, which harms even the oppressor. Yet dawah is never irrelevant: nothing in history has been more impactful, and the diverse congregation before him is its fruit. From Surah Ibrahim he draws two points. First, Musa was sent to bring his people from darkness into light, so Muslims must see the rulings as Allah's path to enlightenment for their own benefit, not a list of rules. You cannot call others to a light you do not live; you need not be perfect, but it must reach your own soul first, since the light needed on the Day of Judgment is built here. Second, every messenger spoke his people's language, which means knowing your audience and calling with wisdom and courtesy. The Prophet's gentleness with the Bedouin who urinated in the masjid and with a rude man, explained through the parable of the runaway camel, shows how. Nuh's report to Allah shows that the quality of the message matters, not just the effort. Sharing guidance is how we thank Allah for it.

outline.heading: Opening
Dawah: the function of the prophets
outline.gist: This month is about taking on outreach, to Muslims first and then to non-Muslims, and bringing people back to the masjid. Allah gave this function to those He loved most, and after the Prophet it falls on every Muslim; he admits it is hard to speak of it while the Holy Land bleeds.

outline.heading: Law that binds only people like us
outline.gist: He will not share the lessons of ten months until a ceasefire, but one is certain: international law, courts and human rights matter only when people like us cross a line, never when others do.

outline.heading: Unhealthy even for the oppressor
outline.gist: Such a world is unhealthy for everyone, oppressors included; on the Day of Judgment Allah will tell them they wronged only themselves. Muslim optimism wants to see goodness, but it is hard amid the rubble.

outline.heading: Why dawah still matters
outline.gist: Dawah may seem irrelevant to the cause, but nothing in history has been more impactful; the congregation of every race before him is the fruit of earlier generations' dawah. First point from the opening verses: Allah sent Musa with His signs to bring his people out of darkness into light (14:5).

outline.heading: From darkness into light
outline.gist: Allah gave us light: a way to walk the path and see what lies ahead. If you do not see Islam that way, something is wrong with how you are looking at it; many Muslims carry this flaw for years.

outline.heading: He commands us for us
outline.gist: Allah is neither harmed by our sins nor helped by our good deeds, so His rules exist only because He knows what leads to harm and what leads to peace. Only an enlightened soul reaches the place of His mercy and love.

outline.heading: Show me the tunnel, then the light
outline.gist: We must first see Islam as the only way out of darkness in these dark times; walking in darkness has no benefit, and only seeing the light lets you walk and invite others along.

outline.heading: Calling others while forgetting yourself
outline.gist: If it is full of light, why is it not working for you? Do you enjoin good and forget yourselves while reciting the Book (2:44)? The first step of dawah is embracing the Quran and the Prophet as your own light; you need not be perfect.

outline.heading: Allah never commanded what harms us
outline.gist: Another of Allah's hypotheticals: had He commanded them to kill themselves or leave their homes, few would have obeyed; had they followed what He did command, it would have strengthened and guided them (4:66-68).

outline.heading: Let the light reach your own soul first
outline.gist: If you are not following it, you should feel the darkness and ask to be moved into the light, so you can offer it to others who long for it.

outline.heading: The hypocrites ask for light
outline.gist: At a moment when no one remembers child, parent or spouse, the hypocrites beg the believers to slow down so they can use their light, and are told to go back (57:13).

outline.heading: Light is built in this life
outline.gist: Go back means go back to this world: you cannot buy a flashlight to cross the bridge on that day. Light comes from the Book, and embracing it and spreading it feed each other in a virtuous cycle.

outline.heading: Interlude
Every messenger spoke his people's language
outline.gist: Second point: every messenger was sent in the tongue of his people to make things clear (14:4). The point is not Arabic but proper communication: know your audience or you cannot affect them, as the Prophet knew and taught his companions.

outline.heading: Call with wisdom and good counsel
outline.gist: Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom, kind reminders and the best arguments and manners (16:125), never by offending, judging or repelling people; anyone who doubts it has not studied his life.

outline.heading: The Bedouin who urinated in the masjid
outline.gist: A man urinated in the Prophet's masjid; the Prophet told the companions to sit down, had water poured on it and taught him gently. Years later the man said the Prophet had not scolded, yelled at or shamed him.

outline.heading: The rude man and the runaway camel
outline.gist: A man insulted the Prophet while he gave out wealth; the Prophet gave him more until he was satisfied, then likened the companions to people chasing a runaway camel further away while its owner calls it back with a handful of grass.

outline.heading: The attitude of the language
outline.gist: Know what people need and struggle with, and speak not just their words but their attitude and perspective; if you cannot speak well, there are a million non-verbal ways to give dawah.

outline.heading: Nuh's report to Allah
outline.gist: Asked why he had only 72 followers after years of calling, Nuh tells Allah he called his people night and day, openly and privately, and told them how much Allah forgives and that He would open the skies for them (71:5-12).

outline.heading: Show me the quality of your work
outline.gist: Allah asked not only how much Nuh called but what he said; if Nuh must account for the quality of his message, so must we. He restates the two points: embrace the light yourself, and speak so people understand.

outline.heading: Sharing guidance as gratitude
outline.gist: Guidance is the most valuable gift in the world and was given free; the way to thank Allah for it is to help others see it.

outline.heading: Outro

66:3.ar: وَإِذۡ أَسَرَّ ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضِ أَزۡوَٰجِهِۦ حَدِيثࣰ ا فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتۡ بِهِۦ وَأَظۡهَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ عَرَّفَ بَعۡضَهُۥ وَأَعۡرَضَ عَنۢ بَعۡضࣲۖ فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَهَا بِهِۦ قَالَتۡ مَنۡ أَنۢبَأَكَ هَٰذَاۖ قَالَ نَبَّأَنِيَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
66:3.en: When the Prophet confided a fact unto one of his wives and when she afterward divulged it and Allah apprised him thereof, he made known (to her) part thereof and passed over part. And when he told it her she said: Who hath told thee? He said: The Knower, the Aware hath told me

66:4.ar: إِن تَتُوبَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ صَغَتۡ قُلُوبُكُمَاۖ وَإِن تَظَٰهَرَا عَلَيۡهِ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰهُ وَجِبۡرِيلُ وَصَٰلِحُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَۖ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ
66:4.en: If ye twain turn unto Allah repentant, (ye have cause to do so) for your hearts desired (the ban); and if ye aid one another against him (Muhammad) then lo! Allah, even He, is his Protecting Friend, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers; and furthermore the angels are his helpers

66:5.ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّهُۥٓ إِن طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَن يُبۡدِلَهُۥٓ أَزۡوَٰجًا خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنكُنَّ مُسۡلِمَٰتࣲ مُّؤۡمِنَٰتࣲ قَٰنِتَٰتࣲ تَٰٓئِبَٰتٍ عَٰبِدَٰتࣲ سَٰٓئِحَٰتࣲ ثَيِّبَٰتࣲ وَأَبۡكَارࣰ ا
66:5.en: It may happen that his Lord, if he divorce you, will give him in your stead wives better than you, submissive (to Allah), believing, pious, penitent, devout, inclined to fasting, widows and maids

66:6.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَأَهۡلِيكُمۡ نَارࣰ ا وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُ عَلَيۡهَا مَلَٰٓئِكَةٌ غِلَاظࣱ شِدَادࣱ لَّا يَعۡصُونَ ٱللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمۡ وَيَفۡعَلُونَ مَا يُؤۡمَرُونَ
66:6.en: O ye who believe! Ward off from yourselves and your families a Fire whereof the fuel is men and stones, over which are set angels strong, severe, who resist not Allah in that which He commandeth them, but do that which they are commanded

COZdvtivyHE.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Tahrim, Part 2 (66:3-6)
COZdvtivyHE.one_line: Lessons on marriage from the Prophet's handling of a disclosed secret, the traits to seek in a spouse, and protecting one's family from the Fire.
COZdvtivyHE.summary: He frames Al-Tahrim as the surah that organizes the family, the unit on which Muslim society rests, and opens with a long reflection on parenting: children who are shielded from boredom, rejection and disappointment never learn to process those feelings and later reach for addictions. He then stresses that the Quran insisted on the fine details of spousal etiquette at a time when life was so harsh that nobody cared about such things, which shows how much they matter. From the Prophet's response when a confided secret was spread, he draws three lessons: do not deprive yourself needlessly to please a spouse, guard the confidentiality of the home, and stop needing to be right, since the Prophet mentioned only part of what he knew to protect the relationship. On verse 5 he notes the change in verse endings that signals a teaching point for everyone, lists the personality traits Allah names for a spouse (practice, conviction, devotion to the task, love with humility, owning mistakes, flexibility) and argues that previously married or never married makes no difference, criticizing cultural taboos and the delay of marriage in the community. He closes by introducing verse 6 as the central verse of the surah: protect yourselves and your spouse and children from the Fire.

outline.heading: Al-Tahrim as the surah that organizes the family
outline.gist: He places the surah at the end of the series on organizing Muslim society and says healthy families depend on spouses who understand their rights, duties and reasons for marrying.

outline.heading: Do not shelter children from life
outline.gist: Children must experience boredom, rejection and disappointment at home; overprotected and overscheduled children never learn to process these feelings and later fall into anxiety and addiction.

outline.heading: Spousal details were revealed in a harsh era
outline.gist: Islam's focus on spousal conduct builds stable families, and these verses came to people facing high child mortality and a brutal desert life.

outline.heading: Why the context makes these details matter
outline.gist: The Quran insisted on how spouses speak and think of each other when no one had the luxury to care, even with armies marching on Madinah, which shows these details matter.

outline.heading: The secret the Prophet confided and its disclosure
outline.gist: He recounts the honey story: the Prophet swore off it and asked for confidence, the secret was spread, Allah informed him, and he mentioned only part of it to his wife.

outline.heading: Informed by the All-Knowing, the All-Aware
outline.gist: The Prophet answered that Al-Alim Al-Khabir told him; he explains Al-Alim as an umbrella name and Al-Khabir as knowledge of hidden motives and fine details.

outline.heading: Lesson: keep the confidences of the home
outline.gist: Exciting and sad news tempt us to share, but sharing household matters gains little and loses much; outside abuse, what happens between spouses stays there.

outline.heading: Lesson: marriage is not about being right
outline.gist: The Prophet raised only the breach of trust and ignored the plotting; constantly proving a spouse wrong produces a weak partner, a weak parent and a failing household.

outline.heading: The three lessons of verse 3 drawn together
outline.gist: Do not give things up needlessly for a spouse, honour the confidentiality of marriage before and after divorce, and treat marriage as a team where no one rubs in mistakes.

outline.heading: Interlude
Call to the two wives to repent
outline.gist: The verse encourages the two wives to return to Allah because their hearts had leaned away from considering the Prophet.

outline.heading: Allah, Jibril, the righteous and the angels back the Prophet
outline.gist: The verse shows Allah's love for His Prophet: Allah is his protector, and Jibril, the righteous believers and the angels have his back.

outline.heading: A change in verse endings signals a new point
outline.gist: Verse 5 ends differently from its neighbours; such breaks in rhythm, unlike rigid poetry, draw attention to a separate point, and he urges listeners to notice and ask about them.

outline.heading: A hypothetical given as a teaching point for us
outline.gist: The Prophet never divorced his wives and both repented; the hypothetical of better wives is a lesson on what to look for in a spouse.

outline.heading: Previously married or not: cultural taboos are not Islam
outline.gist: Allah lists previously married and never married women together; the stigma against marrying a divorcee is a borrowed Victorian norm, and the Prophet married Khadijah and others who had been married before.

outline.heading: Marriage is being made too hard
outline.gist: Excessive scrutiny, cost and delay leave the community full of unmarried people in their late twenties and thirties, unlike the easier remarriage of the Prophet's time.

outline.heading: Trait: practice with conviction (muslimat, mu'minat)
outline.gist: Seek someone who practises and genuinely believes, not one following inherited habit.

outline.heading: Trait: devotion that finishes the task (qanitat)
outline.gist: Qunut means staying at the job past the required time; seek someone task-oriented rather than a clock-watcher.

outline.heading: Trait: love joined with humility ('abidat)
outline.gist: Ibadah comes from one of the highest degrees of love, combining emotion and humbleness.

outline.heading: Trait: the ability to admit and fix mistakes (ta'ibat)
outline.gist: Repentance here is a personality trait: recognizing when one is wrong and correcting it.

outline.heading: Trait: flexibility (sa'ihat)
outline.gist: The word for travel refers to mental and psychological ease in moving from one position to another; Allah names character, not wealth, beauty or degrees.

outline.heading: The criteria work both ways, and a woman needs a wali
outline.gist: Men and women should seek these traits; a woman also needs a man she trusts to size up a suitor's provision and sincerity.

outline.heading: Raise the young with these traits
outline.gist: We neither seek nor cultivate ownership, humility, admitting mistakes and flexibility in our youth, though life demands them.

outline.heading: Verse 6 as the central verse of the surah
outline.gist: The whole surah builds to this verse, the bottom line on family.

outline.heading: Qu: protect yourselves, from the root of taqwa
outline.gist: The command comes from the root of wiqayah, protection and prevention, the same root as taqwa.

outline.heading: Ahl means spouse and children
outline.gist: In Arabic ahl refers to one's wife and children, not parents, so the command targets the household one heads.

outline.heading: A fire fuelled by people and stones, guarded by stern angels
outline.gist: He describes the fire and its gatekeeper angels who never disobey, to be continued next week.

themes.label: Taqwa and God-consciousness

3:159.ar: فَبِمَا رَحۡمَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلۡقَلۡبِ لَٱنفَضُّواْ مِنۡ حَوۡلِكَۖ فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ وَشَاوِرۡهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمۡتَ فَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
3:159.en: It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah. Lo! Allah loveth those who put their trust (in Him)

3:154.ar: ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡغَمِّ أَمَنَةࣰ نُّعَاسࣰ ا يَغۡشَىٰ طَآئِفَةࣰ مِّنكُمۡۖ وَطَآئِفَةࣱ قَدۡ أَهَمَّتۡهُمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِۖ يَقُولُونَ هَل لَّنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۗ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ كُلَّهُۥ لِلَّهِۗ يُخۡفُونَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِم مَّا لَا يُبۡدُونَ لَكَۖ يَقُولُونَ لَوۡ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ شَيۡءࣱ مَّا قُتِلۡنَا هَٰهُنَاۗ قُل لَّوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُيُوتِكُمۡ لَبَرَزَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَتۡلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمۡۖ وَلِيَبۡتَلِيَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
3:154.en: Then, after grief, He sent down security for you. As slumber did it overcome a party of you, while (the other) party, who were anxious on their own account, thought wrongly of Allah, the thought of ignorance. They said: Have we any part in the cause? Say (O Muhammad): The cause belongeth wholly to Allah. They hide within themselves (a thought) which they reveal not unto thee, saying: Had we had any part in the cause we should not have been slain here. Say: Even though ye had been in your houses, those appointed to be slain would have gone forth to the places where they were to lie. (All this hath been) in order that Allah might try what is in your breasts and prove what is in your hearts. Allah is Aware of what is hidden in the breasts (of men)

3:168.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ لِإِخۡوَٰنِهِمۡ وَقَعَدُواْ لَوۡ أَطَاعُونَا مَا قُتِلُواْۗ قُلۡ فَٱدۡرَءُواْ عَنۡ أَنفُسِكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
3:168.en: Those who, while they sat at home, said of their brethren (who were fighting for the cause of Allah): If they had been guided by us they would not have been slain. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Then avert death from yourselves if ye are truthful

3:156.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَقَالُواْ لِإِخۡوَٰنِهِمۡ إِذَا ضَرَبُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَوۡ كَانُواْ غُزࣰّ ى لَّوۡ كَانُواْ عِندَنَا مَا مَاتُواْ وَمَا قُتِلُواْ لِيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ ذَٰلِكَ حَسۡرَةࣰ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
3:156.en: O ye who believe! Be not as those who disbelieved and said of their brethren who went abroad in the land or were fighting in the field: If they had been (here) with us they would not have died or been killed: that Allah may make it anguish in their hearts. Allah giveth life and causeth death; and Allah is Seer of what ye do

8:43.ar: إِذۡ يُرِيكَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلࣰ اۖ وَلَوۡ أَرَىٰكَهُمۡ كَثِيرࣰ ا لَّفَشِلۡتُمۡ وَلَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَلَّمَۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
8:43.en: When Allah showed them unto thee (O Muhammad) in thy dream as few in number, and if He had shown them to thee as many, ye (Muslims) would have faltered and would have quarrelled over the affair. But Allah saved (you). Lo! He knoweth what is in the breasts (of men)

33:14.ar: وَلَوۡ دُخِلَتۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنۡ أَقۡطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةَ لَأٓتَوۡهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِهَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرࣰ ا
33:14.en: If the enemy had entered from all sides and they had been exhorted to treachery, they would have committed it, and would have hesitated thereupon but little

0KmiaDuHsQU.speaker_note: Same outreach series and format (English first khutbah, Arabic second khutbah); the following week's khutbah (w8zz_zRXjWE) refers back to this 'hypothetical' talk. No other voice.
0KmiaDuHsQU.title: Outreach, The Way of Our Prophets: What If?
0KmiaDuHsQU.one_line: On 'what if': why not to wish you had lived in the Prophet's time, why 'if only' opens Shaytan's door, and how Allah knows who you would have been.
0KmiaDuHsQU.summary: Starting from the helplessness of two billion Muslims watching the Holy Land, he takes up the habit of asking 'what if', especially the wish to have lived with the Prophet. He answers with al-Miqdad's rebuke to a man who said so: you do not know how you would have been, some who saw the Prophet are in the Fire, so thank Allah you were born knowing there is no god but Allah. He warns that 'if only' opens the door to Shaytan, using the Uhud verses where the hypocrites say their brothers would have lived had they stayed home. Yet Allah Himself speaks in hypotheticals: had He shown the Prophet the true size of the army at Badr, the believers would have lost heart; had the Confederates entered from the north, the hypocrites would have given in; had the Prophet been harsh, even the best companions would have scattered. Allah knows what was, is, will be and would have been. If we are still believers, it is because He has drawn His veil over us and has not tested us at our breaking point. So do not boast of your faith; feel ashamed before Him, purify yourself, ask Him for safety, and know you are judged by your daily choices, which show who you would have been.

outline.heading: Opening
Helpless before the Holy Land
outline.gist: Two billion Muslims keep watching helplessly what is happening to the people of the Holy Land; he frames the question of the day within the outreach series.

outline.heading: The wish to have lived with the Prophet
outline.gist: Many imagine that, had they lived in his time and place, they would have stood by him; a companion was once faced with exactly this wish.

outline.heading: Al-Miqdad: you do not know how you would have been
outline.gist: A man told al-Miqdad he wished his eyes had seen what al-Miqdad saw; al-Miqdad replied that some who saw the Prophet with their own eyes were thrown into the Fire, so thank Allah for being born knowing only that there is no god but Allah. He admits he has wondered the same since childhood.

outline.heading: 'If only' opens the door to Shaytan
outline.gist: The hadith of Abu Hurayrah in the Sahih: do not say 'if only I had done such and such', for 'if' opens the work of Shaytan.

outline.heading: The hypocrites' 'if' at Uhud
outline.gist: Those who stayed behind said the dead would have lived had they listened; Allah answers that death would have reached them in their homes, and turns their 'if' into regret in their hearts (3:154, 3:168, 3:156). Allah may speak in 'if'; we may not.

outline.heading: Allah knows what would have been
outline.gist: Allah knows what was, what is, what will be, and what never happened and how it would have been had it happened.

outline.heading: Badr: the army shown as few
outline.gist: Allah showed the Prophet the enemy as few in his dream; had He shown them as many, the believers would have lost heart and quarrelled (8:43). About a thousand men, three hundred of them mounted, against 314 with two horses: no contest on paper.

outline.heading: The Trench: had they entered from the north
outline.gist: The trench held the one open side; had the army of ten thousand entered from the north, the hypocrites would have given in almost at once (33:14).

outline.heading: Had he been harsh
outline.gist: By Allah's mercy the Prophet was gentle; had he been harsh and hard-hearted, even Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, al-Zubayr and Talha would have scattered from him (3:159).

outline.heading: Allah sees the version of you raised elsewhere
outline.gist: Allah sees the version of me that grew up less comfortable financially and socially, in another country, and knows whether I would have held my ground; He sees it fully, not in a way that removes my choice.

outline.heading: My breaking point
outline.gist: It is shameful that He sees my breaking point while I walk around as if my faith were strong; I am only fortunate He has not yet tested me with it, and things could easily have gone the other way.

outline.heading: Interlude
Allah knows who you would have been
outline.gist: In Arabic: Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, knows how we would be in circumstances other than our own. If that does not frighten you, you have not understood; if I am still a believer, it is because He has drawn His veil over me.

outline.heading: Hold your tongue from 'if'
outline.gist: What knowledge do I have to say 'had I done this, that would have happened'? Accept it as Allah's decree, seek forgiveness for your shortcomings, praise Him for what you did not deserve, and move on.

outline.heading: Allah's 'if' humbles us
outline.gist: Allah tells the believers they won, but had the Prophet seen a different number they would have failed, and had the Confederates come from the north they would have fallen; hence the prophets' plea on the Day of Judgment: O Allah, grant safety.

outline.heading: Ashamed before the One who sees
outline.gist: Change one circumstance and I might lose this world and the next. Allah knows how I would have acted in the Prophet's days or in Gaza beside those paying the blood price for us; it is shameful to let Him see this and not purify yourself and draw nearer.

outline.heading: Allah does not need to force anyone
outline.gist: Some argue about predestination, but Allah has no need to force anyone; He knows what we do not.

outline.heading: Judged by your daily choices
outline.gist: His judgment rests on your daily choices and how you live; what you do today shows who you would have been in other times and places, so if you wish you had been with the Prophet, live like it now.

outline.heading: Outro

65:8.ar: وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرۡيَةٍ عَتَتۡ عَنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّهَا وَرُسُلِهِۦ فَحَاسَبۡنَٰهَا حِسَابࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ ا وَعَذَّبۡنَٰهَا عَذَابࣰ ا نُّكۡرࣰ ا
65:8.en: And how many a community revolted against the ordinance of its Lord and His messengers, and We called it to a stern account and punished it with dire punishment

65:9.ar: فَذَاقَتۡ وَبَالَ أَمۡرِهَا وَكَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ أَمۡرِهَا خُسۡرًا
65:9.en: So that it tasted the ill-effects of its conduct, and the consequence of its conduct was loss

65:10.ar: أَعَدَّ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ اۖ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۚ قَدۡ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكُمۡ ذِكۡرࣰ ا
65:10.en: Allah hath prepared for them stern punishment; so keep your duty to Allah, O men of understanding! O ye who believe! Now Allah hath sent down unto you a reminder

65:11.ar: رَّسُولࣰ ا يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ مُبَيِّنَٰتࣲ لِّيُخۡرِجَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِۚ وَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ وَيَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحࣰ ا يُدۡخِلۡهُ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدࣰ اۖ قَدۡ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥ رِزۡقًا
65:11.en: A messenger reciting unto you the revelations of Allah made plain, that He may bring forth those who believe and do good works from darkness unto light. And whosoever believeth in Allah and doeth right, He will bring him into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, therein to abide for ever. Allah hath made good provision for him

65:12.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ وَمِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِثۡلَهُنَّۖ يَتَنَزَّلُ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ بَيۡنَهُنَّ لِتَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ أَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عِلۡمَۢا
65:12.en: Allah it is who hath created seven heavens, and of the earth the like thereof. The commandment cometh down among them slowly, that ye may know that Allah is Able to do all things, and that Allah surroundeth all things in knowledge

33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled

16:58.ar: وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم بِٱلۡأُنثَىٰ ظَلَّ وَجۡهُهُۥ مُسۡوَدࣰّ ا وَهُوَ كَظِيمࣱ‏
16:58.en: When if one of them receiveth tidings of the birth of a female, his face remaineth darkened, and he is wroth inwardly

16:59.ar: يَتَوَٰرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ مِن سُوٓءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِۦٓۚ أَيُمۡسِكُهُۥ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمۡ يَدُسُّهُۥ فِي ٱلتُّرَابِۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَحۡكُمُونَ
16:59.en: He hideth himself from the folk because of the evil of that whereof he hath had tidings, (asking himself): Shall he keep it in contempt, or bury it beneath the dust. Verily evil is their judgment

16:60.ar: لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مَثَلُ ٱلسَّوۡءِۖ وَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡمَثَلُ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
16:60.en: For those who believe not in the Hereafter is an evil similitude, and Allah's is the Sublime Similitude. He is the Mighty, the Wise

YIqANY0f7vk.speaker_note: His own Monday tafseer series, concluding the surah
YIqANY0f7vk.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Talaq, Part 4 (65:8-12)
YIqANY0f7vk.one_line: Compatibility and qiwamah in marriage, then the surah's closing warnings: why Allah threatens those who return to the oppression of women.
YIqANY0f7vk.summary: After recapping the series and the cluster of organizational surahs, he finishes his marriage advice. Compatibility in religion, finances and social norms matters because early attraction changes and blurs judgment; parents who know their child, if free of racial or cultural bias, are good judges, and checking compatibility first avoids a painful choice between a spouse and family. Qiwamah means protection and provision, never control, matched by the wife following reasonable decisions, and expectations about safety, travel and work should be settled before marriage. He then explains why verses 8 to 12 contain no rulings but heavy warnings: before Islam women were thrown out, unsupported, married without witnesses and their children disowned, and in a lawless land weak fathers even buried daughters. Islam's reforms protected women, and he argues the modern West is no better: pornography and objectification desensitize men, give them endless options, and leave women less secure in marriage. Nations that defy Allah's commands taste the consequences in this life before punishment in the next, so those with intellect must take these laws seriously; the Messenger was sent to bring people from darkness to light, and sexual ethics are a core difference with Western society. The surah ends with Allah, Creator of seven heavens and earths, who knows what works for us.

outline.heading: The goal of the series: the last four juz
outline.gist: Half a page a week covers the last four juz, which summarize most of the Quran; the first group of surahs presented life's basic forks in the road.

outline.heading: The organizational surahs recapped
outline.gist: He reviews how each Madani surah organized relationships with Muslims, citizens, non-Muslims and leaders, with one surah reminding us why we do it all.

outline.heading: Compatibility: Zayd and Zaynab
outline.gist: Being Muslim and liking each other is not enough; two of the greatest companions could not make their marriage work for lack of compatibility.

outline.heading: Early attraction blurs vision
outline.gist: Attraction changes in nature after the first year, and only compatibility in goals and expectations carries the marriage.

outline.heading: The wisdom of parents
outline.gist: Parents who know you can judge whether someone will make you happy, provided they are free of bias.

outline.heading: Financial compatibility
outline.gist: A husband must provide the standard his wife had at home, including a maid if she had one, so mismatched finances rarely work.

outline.heading: Social compatibility: in-laws and food
outline.gist: Different norms mean years of exhausting expectations at Eid and with in-laws, down to food that disagrees with you; he does not advise marrying outside one's culture.

outline.heading: When kafa'ah becomes a cover for racism
outline.gist: Parents sometimes hide prejudice behind compatibility; the actual problem must be stated clearly.

outline.heading: The rookie move
outline.gist: Falling for someone for years before checking both families' acceptance forces someone to lose either a spouse or family.

outline.heading: Stack the odds; don't roll the dice
outline.gist: No marriage is guaranteed, but choosing piety, family, social and financial fit and parental approval protects future children.

outline.heading: Qiwamah is protection and provision, not control
outline.gist: The man is responsible for protecting and providing; the wife follows his reasonable decisions in her interest; neither may dominate or abuse.

outline.heading: Every institution needs a job description
outline.gist: Spouses must clarify who does what, and a woman should ask a suitor what her safety means to him.

outline.heading: Local norms and personal comfort
outline.gist: Here a Muslim woman drives freely within the city; for travel abroad there is no norm, so the husband's comfort must be agreed upon beforehand.

outline.heading: Work and the words husbands use
outline.gist: Objections to a wife working must be raised before marriage; 'I don't want you to' differs from 'I don't think you're safe'.

outline.heading: The rest of the surah: warnings, not rulings
outline.gist: Verses 8 to 12 contain no rulings, and he will explain why Allah ends with heavy warnings.

outline.heading: Interlude
How many towns defied their Lord
outline.gist: Ka'ayyin magnifies the number of nations that arrogantly turned away; the tone shifts from rulings to a Makki-style warning.

outline.heading: Jahiliyyah: thrown out, unwitnessed and disowned
outline.gist: Before Islam divorced women were evicted, kept out of spite, and married without contract or witnesses so men could disown their children.

outline.heading: No support during the waiting period
outline.gist: Men stopped spending even on pregnant wives and pressured them to leave, which the earlier verses forbade.

outline.heading: Burying daughters in a lawless land
outline.gist: Infant burial was not widespread, but where there was no law a weak father felt his daughter was better dead than unprotected.

outline.heading: The face that darkens at news of a daughter
outline.gist: The Quran describes the father hiding in shame; no man of Quraysh buried a daughter because their status protected them, while the weak suffered.

outline.heading: Islam's social reform and why some rejected it
outline.gist: Many resisted Islam for giving rights to the poor, slaves and women, who could no longer be inherited like property.

outline.heading: The West is no better
outline.gist: Women here go unmarried into their thirties, whereas the companions remarried quickly because marriage was easy and obligations clear.

outline.heading: The blue whale in the room: desensitized men
outline.gist: A man sees more nudity in five minutes than his grandfather in a lifetime; secular research shows men preferring screens to spouses.

outline.heading: Bad for women and men alike
outline.gist: Jahiliyyah was bad for women but fine for men; today neither does well, so families suffer.

outline.heading: Chip away at the family and faith goes with it
outline.gist: When marriage is hard to enter, keep and replace, the unit that passes on Islam erodes.

outline.heading: Is objectification in women's interest?
outline.gist: Endless availability and impossible beauty standards serve men who want ease without commitment, sold to women as liberation.

outline.heading: What men want by nature
outline.gist: Men do not naturally seek lifelong commitment, so society must make marriage the path and restrict easy alternatives.

outline.heading: Options make husbands unreasonable
outline.gist: A man who can satisfy himself elsewhere stops compromising with his wife, and marriages end over nothing.

outline.heading: Couples therapy has become a different science
outline.gist: Problems once rare are now the norm; he holds today is no better than jahiliyyah, and Muslims hold the solution.

outline.heading: Punishment through consequences in this life
outline.gist: The severe reckoning is not an asteroid but living the outcomes of one's choices until everything ends in loss.

outline.heading: Oppressed without knowing it
outline.gist: Women in jahiliyyah knew they were oppressed; in the West people believe they are free, as he contrasts with life in Syria.

outline.heading: Interlude
Severe punishment awaits in the Hereafter too
outline.gist: The previous verses described worldly loss, misery and dysfunction; verse 10 adds the punishment of Judgment Day.

outline.heading: Taqwa once more as prevention
outline.gist: Again he is told to keep Allah's displeasure in mind before deciding, to avoid a future of loss.

outline.heading: O people of intellect who believe
outline.gist: Anyone with a mind and faith must take the laws of marriage and divorce seriously.

outline.heading: A reminder in the form of a Messenger
outline.gist: The Messenger and his clear, clarifying verses were sent so people would not regress to mistreating women.

outline.heading: From darkness to light
outline.gist: The phrase appears rarely and recurs where the Quran addresses false accusations of women, tying enlightenment to sexual ethics.

outline.heading: Sexual ethics as a core difference with the West
outline.gist: Muslims see these matters as moral, not merely legal, and must be clearer about where they disagree.

outline.heading: The right not to have children indoctrinated
outline.gist: Without discriminating against anyone, Muslims must claim the right to hold their morality and protect their children's beliefs.

outline.heading: Gardens and excellent provision
outline.gist: Those who believe and do good enter eternal gardens; the verses move from warning to promise.

outline.heading: Losing ground
outline.gist: Weaker households, later and fewer marriages and smaller families show we did not heed these warnings.

outline.heading: Interlude
Creator of seven heavens and as many earths
outline.gist: Allah establishes His credibility: His command descends through all of creation.

outline.heading: He knows what works for you
outline.gist: The Omnipotent and All-Knowing knows what benefits people, so His rulings must be trusted.

outline.heading: The most powerful warning after commands in the Quran
outline.gist: No other set of commands ends with such warnings of loss in both worlds, addressed to thinking believers.

outline.heading: Outro
